summary: A look at Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin's private life: his abusive Georgian childhood, the 1907 Tiflis robbery, his wife's 1932 suicide and the all-night drinking dinners through which he ruled the USSR until his death in 1953.
keywords: In the Court of the Red Tsar

evidence.note: Host frames the episode as everything except Stalin at work: play, dinners, movies
Birth in Gori and abusive childhood open a youth segment of roughly ten minutes
Tiflis stagecoach robbery with bombs to fund the Bolsheviks, dozens killed
1932 banquet quarrel with Nadezhda, followed by her suicide that night
Stalin kicking his pregnant first wife and his violent temper at home
Stalin separates himself from the Stalin of newspapers and portraits
Nightly film screenings, his film curator, propaganda films shaping his view of the famine
Postwar nightly drinking dinners 1945-1953 where state business was settled
Stroke after a night of drinking and death in 1953 close the story

notes: partial_life set: the host explicitly frames the bonus episode around Stalin's private side and skips his work (purges, famine, war only as background). covered_span is still 1878-1953 because the youth segment and death both get real airtime. main_span uses his rule, 1924-1953. Tiflis robbery is under two minutes: kept as role, not as terrorism theme. Famine mentioned only in passing: no genocide theme or mass-atrocity warning.
